ai.literal: Sweet words, love having mixed, deceit they are without; righteousness those who have seen - of their mouth, the word.
ai.translation: The words from the mouths of those who have grasped true righteousness are sweet, filled with love, and free from deceit.
ai.modern: உண்மையான அறத்தை உணர்ந்தவர்களின் வாயிலிருந்து வரும் சொற்கள், அன்பு கலந்ததாகவும் வஞ்சனை இல்லாததாகவும் இருக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines what constitutes truly sweet speech. It is not merely pleasant sounding, but must be mixed with genuine love ('ஈரம்') and be completely free from deceit ('படிறு'). Such pure and kind words naturally flow from the mouths of those who have understood true righteousness ('செம்பொருள்').

ai.literal: Heart being pleased than giving, it is better indeed, face being pleased sweet-worded-one to be if obtained.
ai.translation: It is even better than giving with a joyful heart, if one can speak sweet words with a cheerful face.
ai.modern: உள்ளம் மகிழ்ந்து ஒரு பொருளைக் கொடுப்பதை விட, முகம் மலர்ந்து இனிய சொற்களைக் கூறுபவனாக இருக்க முடிந்தால் அது மிகவும் நல்லது.
ai.explanation: This couplet compares two virtuous acts: giving generously and speaking sweetly. The phrase 'அகன் அமர்ந்து ஈதல்' refers to giving a gift with a willing, joyful heart. However, the poet states that 'முகன் அமர்ந்து இன்சொலன் ஆகப் பெறின்'—having a cheerful face and speaking pleasant words—is even better. The comparative suffix 'இன்' in 'ஈதலின்' combined with 'நன்றே' (it is better indeed) establishes that sweet speech with a smiling face surpasses even heartfelt charity. This emphasizes that kind words are a supreme virtue, accessible to everyone and deeply impactful.

ai.literal: With the face having settled, sweetly having looked, from the heart arising sweet word - of such nature indeed is virtue.
ai.translation: Virtue is simply this: looking sweetly with a welcoming face and speaking sweet words that arise genuinely from the heart.
ai.modern: முகம் மலர்ந்து இனிமையாகப் பார்த்து, உள்ளத்திலிருந்து எழும் இனிய சொற்களைச் சொல்வதே அறமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines virtue in the context of daily human interaction. It states that true virtue consists of a welcoming face, a sweet look, and pleasant words. Crucially, these sweet words must arise genuinely from the heart, as indicated by the word 'அகத்தான்' (from the inside/heart). The combination of a joyful face and sincere, kind words embodies the essence of moral goodness.

ai.literal: Sorrow-causing poverty non-existent will become, towards everyone joy-causing sweet words to them.
ai.translation: Sorrowful poverty will not exist for those who speak sweet words that bring joy to everyone.
ai.modern: யாரிடத்திலும் மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தரும் இனிய சொற்களைப் பேசுபவர்களுக்கு, துன்பத்தைத் தரும் வறுமை இல்லாமல் போகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet states that those who habitually speak sweet words that bring joy to everyone they meet will never suffer from the pain of poverty. The word 'துவ்வாமை' literally means the inability to enjoy or consume, which signifies destitution. By contrasting 'துன்புறூஉம்' (sorrow-causing) with 'இன்புறூஉம்' (joy-causing), the poet emphasizes that giving joy through words naturally dispels one's own sorrowful lack.

ai.literal: Possessor of humility, speaker of sweet words being, to a person ornament; are not besides other things.
ai.translation: Being humble and speaking sweet words are the true ornaments for a person; all other things are not.
ai.modern: ஒருவருக்கு உண்மையான அணிகலன்கள் பணிவுடையவராகவும் இனிய சொற்களைப் பேசுபவராகவும் இருப்பதே ஆகும்; மற்றவை எல்லாம் அணிகலன்கள் ஆகா.
ai.explanation: This couplet defines the true adornment for any individual. It states that possessing humility and speaking sweet words are the only real ornaments for a person. The phrase 'மற்றுப் பிற' (all other things) combined with 'அல்ல' (are not) dismisses physical jewelry or external decorations as false ornaments. The word 'ஆதல்' (being) emphasizes that these are internal qualities one must embody, rather than external objects one wears.

ai.literal: Evil things to diminish, virtue will increase, good things having sought, if pleasant (words) one speaks.
ai.translation: If one seeks out good things and speaks pleasant words, their sins will diminish and their virtue will increase.
ai.modern: நன்மையானவைகளை ஆராய்ந்து இனிமையான சொற்களைச் சொன்னால், ஒருவருடைய பாவங்கள் குறைந்து அறம் பெருகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet explains the moral benefits of speaking kindly. It says that when a person actively seeks out good thoughts and speaks pleasant words, the negative aspects of their life will wear away. At the same time, their virtue and righteousness will naturally grow. The words 'தேய' (diminish) and 'பெருகும்' (increase) create a powerful contrast, showing how good speech replaces evil with virtue.

ai.literal: Agreeableness having yielded, goodness it will produce; benefit having yielded, from character not departing word.
ai.translation: Words that yield practical benefit and never depart from good character will bring forth joy and produce lasting goodness.
ai.modern: பயனைத் தந்து நல்ல பண்பிலிருந்து விலகாத சொற்கள், கேட்பவருக்கு மகிழ்ச்சியைத் தந்து நன்மையை உண்டாக்கும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet describes the dual positive effects of speaking sweet, character-driven words. The subject is words that yield practical benefit (பயன்) and never depart from good character (பண்பு). The predicate states that such words will bring forth immediate joy or agreeableness (நயன்) and produce lasting goodness (நன்றி). The repetition of the word 'ஈன்று' (having yielded) emphasizes that good words are fertile and productive, bearing fruit in both usefulness and emotional warmth.

ai.literal: From meanness freed sweet word, in the next birth too, in this birth too, happiness will give.
ai.translation: Sweet words freed from all meanness will bring happiness in this birth and the next.
ai.modern: குற்றமற்ற இனிய சொற்கள் ஒருவனுக்கு இந்தப் பிறவியிலும் அடுத்த பிறவியிலும் இன்பத்தைத் தரும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet highlights the enduring power of speaking kindly and without malice. The phrase 'சிறுமையுவு நீங்கிய' emphasizes that true sweet words must be free from deceit, harm, or petty intentions. When a person speaks such pure and pleasant words, it yields joy and good outcomes not only in their current life but also in the life to come.

ai.literal: Sweet word sweet thing yielding he-who-sees, why I-wonder harsh word using?
ai.translation: When a person sees that sweet words yield sweet results, why would he use harsh words?
ai.modern: இனிய சொற்கள் இன்பத்தைத் தருவதைக் காணும் ஒருவன், கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுவது ஏனோ?
ai.explanation: The couplet contrasts the effects of sweet and harsh words. The word 'காண்பான்' (he who sees) emphasizes personal experience: the speaker already knows firsthand that sweet words produce joy ('இனிது ஈன்றல்'). Given this clear evidence, the poet wonders ('எவன்கொலோ') why anyone would choose to speak harsh words ('வன்சொல்'). It highlights the irrationality of choosing harshness when the benefits of kindness are obvious.

ai.literal: Sweet things while existing, unpleasant things saying, ripe fruit while being, unripe fruit having grasped like that.
ai.translation: Speaking harsh words when sweet words are available is like choosing to eat unripe fruit when ripe fruit is at hand.
ai.modern: இனிமையான சொற்கள் இருக்கும்போது கடுமையான சொற்களைப் பேசுவது, உண்ணுவதற்கு இனிமையான கனி இருக்கும்போது காயை விரும்பி உண்பதற்குச் சமமாகும்.
ai.explanation: This couplet uses a simple and powerful analogy to contrast sweet and harsh speech. The word 'இனிய' refers to pleasant, kind words, while 'இன்னாத' refers to harsh, hurtful ones. The poet compares choosing harsh words over kind ones to picking an unripe, bitter fruit ('காய்') when a sweet, ripe fruit ('கனி') is readily available. By using the word 'கவர்ந்து' (grasping or desiring), the couplet highlights the foolishness of actively choosing something unpleasant when something delightful is already at hand.
